The **Behringer X32** is our main mixing desk. It has 32 input channels, and every one of them is the same
strip of tools, in the same order. Learn one channel and you know all 32.

## The strip, in order

Press a channel's **Select** button and the knobs in the middle of the desk (the *channel strip*) all work on
that channel. The X32 manual lists its sections in signal order:

1. **Config / Preamp**: **Gain** (how much the mic signal is amplified, −12 to +60 dB), **48 V** phantom power
   for condenser mics, **Ø** polarity flip, and the **Low Cut** filter (20–400 Hz).
2. **Gate** and **Dynamics**: the noise gate turns the channel *down* when it's quiet; the compressor turns the
   loud parts down.
3. **Equalizer**: four bands (Low, Lo Mid, Hi Mid, High), each with Type, Freq, Gain and Q.
4. **Bus Sends** and **Main Bus**: monitor mixes, effects, and the send to the main speakers (pan, and the
   fader at the bottom of the strip).

Each section has a button that switches it on (lit) or off (dark), and a **View** button that opens all its
settings on the screen. The compressor can sit before or after the EQ (the **Pos** setting on the Dyn page).

<div class="sk-tip">On the fader strip itself you also get <b>Mute</b>, <b>Solo</b>, a small input meter, and
two little lights that show when the <b>gate</b> and <b>compressor</b> are working on that channel.</div>

## Try it: one X32 channel

This is one channel of the X32, laid out left to right instead of top to bottom. The knobs have the X32's
ranges. Drag a knob up or down (Shift for fine), use the mouse wheel or the arrow keys; double-click to reset.

<div class="lk" data-w="strip" data-source="vocal" data-goal="auto"></div>

- **Speakers** is *your* volume, not part of the desk.
- The **input meter** next to Gain shows the level after the preamp, with the X32's marks (−54 to clip).
- The graph under the EQ shows the EQ curve (amber) over what is coming out (blue).
- The strip at the bottom shows the last 4 seconds: grey is the level the gate sees, amber what comes out,
  and dashed lines for the gate and compressor thresholds when they're on.
- **⤓ WAV** saves the source sound so you can play it through the real desk (see
  [Live Sound 7](live-soundcheck.qmd#practice-on-the-real-x32)).

Every source here has something wrong with it on purpose. The next lessons fix them one at a time.

## Gain is not volume

The single most common mistake on a live desk: using the **Gain** knob as a volume control, or the fader as
a fix for bad gain. They do different jobs. [Live Sound 2](live-gain.qmd) is all about it.
